subject.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing

question: Should a missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef become a cold-start-only fail-open exception to the active SecretRef contract?
rationale: Current documentation deliberately makes effectively active SecretRefs startup-fatal, so accepting an optional-capability exception requires explicit product and security-boundary ownership beyond correcting the line-level lifecycle bug.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow exception
options.body: Allow missing-value-only degradation during the first activating Gateway startup while preserving strict reload, restart-check, and write preflight behavior.

options.title: Keep universal fail-fast
options.body: Preserve the existing active-SecretRef contract and decline credential-class exceptions in shared startup handling.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow exception
recommendation.body: Allow missing-value-only degradation during the first activating Gateway startup while preserving strict reload, restart-check, and write preflight behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the SecretRef runtime and activation lifecycle whose policy this PR changes.
